Temperature-controlled logistics

Passing every KPI and still failing the customer

How a temperature-controlled network moved revised KPI performance from 82% to 99.1% and reduced quarantine events.

82%starting SLA performance
99.1%revised KPI performance
9 monthsto the revised result
Near-zeroquarantine events after 3 months

The situation

A European temperature-controlled logistics specialist was running at 82% against its contracted SLA framework, generating service credits and active client reviews.

The score was real. The question was whether it was locating the cause.

What the journey showed

Consignments could be on time and within the contracted range while exceeding a product-specific handling threshold. The SLA recorded success while the client quarantined the delivery. Hub dwell in two markets was associated with the transit-stage excursion pattern.

The rebuild

The measurement framework incorporated product-profile thresholds, pack types were reviewed for the affected markets and hub dwell received a maximum processing window.

Measured result

Performance on the revised framework moved from 82% to 99.1% over nine months. Client quarantine events fell to near-zero within the first three months after the hub protocol change.

Historical operator track record. Company name withheld. Metrics and factual framing follow the confirmed September 2026 case-study source.
